Priya —

Summary of legal view and suggested compromise below. Short answer: we should avoid broad carve-outs for lost profits or "regulatory fines" without explicit caps and narrow triggers. But we can accept a limited exception for direct, reasonably foreseeable losses tied to service outages or data destruction if we: (i) limit to a specific subset of services, (ii) keep an explicit monetary cap tied to fees, and (iii) exclude punitive/regulatory penalties unless caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Draft proposal (to send to Horizon as clean language):

"Limitation of Liability. Except for liability arising from (a) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) Redwood's breach of its confidentiality obligations, and (c) Redwood's failure to comply with applicable data protection laws, each party's aggregate liability for direct damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the total Fees paid or payable by Customer under the Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (ii) $1,000,000. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for direct damages resulting from a Redwood service outage that prevents access to mission-critical functionality for more than twenty-four (24) consecutive hours, Customer's aggregate liability cap for such outage-related direct damages shall be the greater of (x) the Fees for the affected service(s) for the twelve (12) months following the outage, or (y) $2,500,000. Except as set forth above, neither party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, consequential, special or exemplary damages (including lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, or loss of goodwill), whether in contract, tort or otherwise, even if advised of the possibility of such damages."

Why this works: it keeps a general exclusion of consequential damages (preserves predictability) but acknowledges a narrow, time-limited outage exception with a higher cap. We include a higher fallback amount to create room for negotiation. We also tie exceptions to gross negligence for regulatory fines (so Horizon can't shift regulatory exposure to us absent egregious conduct).

Draft redline file: Redwood-damages-clause-examples.pdf attached — contains three alternate formulations: (A) conservative (no outage exception), (B) compromise (above), (C) commercial (higher cap + limited consequential carve-out for revenue loss with strict definition).

If Sales is ok with Option B, I can send a tracked redline + short cover note.

- Marissa

Karen — thanks for the quick turnaround and for flagging Horizon's priorities. We took a close look with Legal and Sales and propose the following compromise to put on the table in tomorrow's negotiation: please see the highlighted language below and attached tracked changes.

Proposed compromise language (clean):

"Limitation of Liability. Except for liability arising from (i) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (ii) Redwood's breach of its confidentiality obligations, and (iii) Redwood's failure to comply with applicable data protection laws, each party's aggregate liability for direct damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (A) the total Fees paid or payable by Customer under the Order Form during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (B) $1,000,000.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, for direct damages resulting solely from a Redwood outage that: (a) directly impacts the Customer's Appointment Booking API ("Critical Booking Service"); and (b) prevents Customer access to the Critical Booking Service for more than twenty-four (24) consecutive hours, Customer's aggregate liability cap for such outage-related direct damages shall be the greater of (x) the Fees attributable to the Critical Booking Service for the twelve (12) months following the outage, or (y) $2,000,000. Prior to pursuing any claim for outage-related direct damages, Customer must: (1) have exhausted available SLA credits for the affected service(s) as set forth in Schedule X; and (2) provide Redwood with written notice and reasonable opportunity to remediate.

Except as set forth above, neither party shall be liable for any indirect, incidental, consequential, special or exemplary damages (including lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, or loss of goodwill), whether in contract, tort or otherwise, even if advised of the possibility of such damages."

Key points: (1) we narrowed the outage exception to a named, mission-critical API (addressing Horizon's booking revenue concern), (2) added an SLA-credit precondition to reduce exposure, and (3) lowered the special outage cap from $2.5M to $2.0M as a commercial concession. We also left regulatory fines tied to gross negligence/willful misconduct only.

Attached: tracked redline (Horizon_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a one-page cover note summarizing tradeoffs. Happy to jump on a quick call with Horizon + Jacob if you want us to walk through the language live.

Best,
